spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m2p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Drones, MaxRound

VARIABLES phase, round, pendingVote, prepRound, cleared

vars == <<phase, round, pendingVote, prepRound, cleared>>

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ round = 0
    /\ pendingVote = [d \in Drones |-> -1]
    /\ prepRound = [d \in Drones |-> -1]
    /\ cleared = {}

BeginRound ==
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "committed"}
    /\ round < MaxRound
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ round' = round + 1
    /\ cleared' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pendingVote, prepRound>>

CastVote(d) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ pendingVote[d] = -1
    /\ pendingVote' = [pendingVote EXCEPT ![d] = round]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, round, prepRound, cleared>>

CastStale(d, r) ==
    /\ r >= 0
    /\ r < round
    /\ pendingVote[d] = -1
    /\ pendingVote' = [pendingVote EXCEPT ![d] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, round, prepRound, cleared>>

ProcessVote(d) ==
    /\ pendingVote[d] # -1
    /\ pendingVote[d] = round
    /\ prepRound' = [prepRound EXCEPT ![d] = round]
    /\ pendingVote' = [pendingVote EXCEPT ![d] = -1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, round, cleared>>

DropVote(d) ==
    /\ pendingVote[d] # -1
    /\ pendingVote[d] # round
    /\ pendingVote' = [pendingVote EXCEPT ![d] = -1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, round, prepRound, cleared>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ phase' = "committed"
    /\ cleared' = {d \in Drones : prepRound[d] = round}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<round, pendingVote, prepRound>>

Next ==
    \/ BeginRound
    \/ Commit
    \/ \E d \in Drones : CastVote(d) \/ ProcessVote(d) \/ DropVote(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones, r \in 0..MaxRound : CastStale(d, r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ClearedVotedThisRound ==
    \A d \in Drones : (d \in cleared) => (prepRound[d] = round)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {d1, d2}
    MaxRound = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ClearedVotedThisRound
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm commits coordinated retardant drops
through two-phase commit, and only drones that prepared (voted yes) in the
current committed transaction are authorized to act; a drone from an
earlier or aborted transaction is stale, and a drone that never prepared
is unauthorized. Transactions proceed in rounds: beginning a round bumps
the round number and clears the prior authorization set. During voting a
drone casts a yes vote tagged with the current round. Because vote messages
travel over a lossy radio mesh they can be reordered: a drone's pending
vote may carry the current round, or a late-arriving old message may leave
a pending vote tagged with an earlier round. The coordinator processes a
pending vote only when its tag matches the current round, recording that
drone's prepare-round; a pending vote whose tag does not match the current
round is dropped as stale. Committing authorizes exactly the drones whose
recorded prepare-round is the current round.

The system model has these actions: BeginRound (bump the round and clear
authorizations), CastVote (a drone leaves a current-round pending vote),
CastStale (a reordered old message leaves an earlier-round pending vote),
ProcessVote (record a current-round pending vote as prepared), DropVote
(discard a pending vote whose round does not match), and Commit (authorize
exactly the drones prepared in the current round).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every drone authorized to act has a recorded prepare-round
equal to the current round, so no stale or unauthorized drone is ever
cleared to drop retardant.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m4p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Students, Workers, QCap

VARIABLES open, queue, enrolled, slow

vars == <<open, queue, enrolled, slow>>

Init ==
    /\ open = Students
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ enrolled = {}
    /\ slow = {}

Submit(s) ==
    /\ s \in open
    /\ s \notin queue
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < QCap
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, enrolled, slow>>

Withdraw(s) ==
    /\ s \in queue
    /\ queue' = queue \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, enrolled, slow>>

Enroll(w, s) ==
    /\ w \notin slow
    /\ s \in queue
    /\ s \in open
    /\ enrolled' = enrolled \cup {s}
    /\ open' = open \ {s}
    /\ queue' = queue \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED slow

BecomeSlow(w) ==
    /\ w \notin slow
    /\ slow' = slow \cup {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, queue, enrolled>>

SpeedUp(w) ==
    /\ w \in slow
    /\ slow' = slow \ {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, queue, enrolled>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Students : Submit(s) \/ Withdraw(s)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, s \in Students : Enroll(w, s)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : BecomeSlow(w) \/ SpeedUp(w)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

EnrollIrreversible ==
    enrolled \cap open = {}
====
nl:
A university course-registration system enrolls students into a course
through a bounded work queue with backpressure. Enrolling a student is an
irreversible action that must happen at most once per student. Students
start out open (eligible to enroll). A registration request may be
submitted into the work queue only while the queue is below its capacity;
when the queue is full, backpressure blocks further submissions until it
drains. A queued request may be withdrawn before it is processed. Workers
pull requests from the queue: a non-slow worker processes a queued request
for a still-open student, which irreversibly enrolls that student and
permanently removes them from the open pool, so they can never be enrolled
again. A worker may be slow but never fails: while slow it cannot process
requests, but it can always speed back up, so it is only delayed.

The system model has these actions: Submit (queue an open student's
request while the queue is below capacity), Withdraw (remove a queued
request before it is processed), Enroll (a non-slow worker irreversibly
enrolls a queued, still-open student and removes them from the open pool),
BecomeSlow (a worker becomes temporarily slow), and SpeedUp (a slow worker
recovers).

SAFETY PROPERTY: No student who has been enrolled is still in the open
pool, so the irreversible enroll action can never be applied to the same
student twice.

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Tasks = {t1, t2, t3}
    QCap = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT TasksConserved
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm processes a fixed set of surveillance
tasks through a bounded work queue with backpressure. Every task is always
in exactly one of four stages -- backlog (not yet queued), queue (waiting
in the bounded work queue), active (picked up by a drone), or completed --
and tasks are never created or destroyed, only moved between stages, so the
grand total is constant. A task may be enqueued from the backlog only while
the queue is below its capacity; when the queue is full, backpressure
blocks further enqueues. Because drones pull tasks over a lossy mesh, tasks
can be picked up out of order (reordered) from the queue. A queued task may
also be dequeued back to the backlog to relieve pressure. An active task is
finished into the completed stage, and a completed task may be reissued
back to the backlog for a fresh sweep.

The system model has these actions: Enqueue (move a backlog task into the
queue while below capacity), Dequeue (return a queued task to the backlog),
Pickup (a drone takes a queued task, in any order), Finish (an active task
becomes completed), and Reissue (a completed task returns to the backlog).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of tasks summed across the backlog, queue,
active, and completed stages always equals the fixed total number of tasks,
so no surveillance task is ever created or destroyed.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m3p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS MatchNodes, Slots, Players, NoNode, Free

VARIABLES leader, assignee, freePool, online, down

vars == <<leader, assignee, freePool, online, down>>

Init ==
    /\ leader = NoNode
    /\ assignee = [s \in Slots |-> Free]
    /\ freePool = Slots
    /\ online = Slots
    /\ down = {}

Elect(c) ==
    /\ leader = NoNode
    /\ c \notin down
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assignee, freePool, online, down>>

StepDown ==
    /\ leader # NoNode
    /\ leader' = NoNode
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assignee, freePool, online, down>>

Allocate(s, p) ==
    /\ leader # NoNode
    /\ s \in online
    /\ s \in freePool
    /\ assignee' = [assignee EXCEPT ![s] = p]
    /\ freePool' = freePool \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, online, down>>

Release(s) ==
    /\ assignee[s] # Free
    /\ assignee' = [assignee EXCEPT ![s] = Free]
    /\ freePool' = IF s \in online THEN freePool \cup {s} ELSE freePool
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, online, down>>

BringOnline(s) ==
    /\ s \notin online
    /\ online' = online \cup {s}
    /\ freePool' = IF assignee[s] = Free THEN freePool \cup {s} ELSE freePool
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, assignee, down>>

TakeOffline(s) ==
    /\ s \in online
    /\ assignee[s] = Free
    /\ online' = online \ {s}
    /\ freePool' = freePool \ {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, assignee, down>>

Crash(c) ==
    /\ c \notin down
    /\ down' = down \cup {c}
    /\ leader' = IF leader = c THEN NoNode ELSE leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<assignee, freePool, online>>

Next ==
    \/ StepDown
    \/ \E c \in MatchNodes : Elect(c) \/ Crash(c)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Release(s) \/ BringOnline(s) \/ TakeOffline(s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, p \in Players : Allocate(s, p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

FreeSlotsAreUnassigned ==
    \A s \in Slots : (s \in freePool) => (assignee[s] = Free)
====
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker assigns players to match slots, using
leader election with failover to decide which node currently drives
assignment. Each slot's assignee field holds either a player or a Free
marker, and a parallel free pool tracks which slots are open. Allocating a
slot to a player stamps the slot's assignee and removes the slot from the
free pool in the same step, so a slot that is currently assigned is never
still in the free pool, which is what prevents the same slot from being
handed to two players. The current leader performs allocations; a leader
may step down, and a node may crash, vacating leadership so a failover
election can pick a new leader. The number of in-service slots is the
capacity and changes at runtime: a slot can be brought online (rejoining
the free pool if unassigned) or, while unassigned, taken offline.

The system model has these actions: Elect (a node becomes leader when
there is none), StepDown (the leader relinquishes leadership), Allocate
(the leader assigns a free, online slot to a player and removes it from the
free pool), Release (an assigned slot is freed and rejoins the pool if
online), BringOnline and TakeOffline (a slot's capacity changes at
runtime), and Crash (a node fails, vacating leadership if it held it).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any slot that sits in the free pool is unassigned, so an
assigned slot is never simultaneously free and can never be double
allocated to two players.

---- MODULE W4Od14m4p5t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Fleets, Targets, QCap, MaxFuel, Idle

VARIABLES backlog, queue, carrying, dropped, fuel

vars == <<backlog, queue, carrying, dropped, fuel>>

Init ==
    /\ backlog = Targets
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ carrying = [f \in Fleets |-> Idle]
    /\ dropped = {}
    /\ fuel = 0

Enqueue(t) ==
    /\ t \in backlog
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < QCap
    /\ backlog' = backlog \ {t}
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carrying, dropped, fuel>>

Pickup(f, t) ==
    /\ carrying[f] = Idle
    /\ t \in queue
    /\ queue' = queue \ {t}
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![f] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, dropped, fuel>>

Drop(f) ==
    /\ carrying[f] # Idle
    /\ carrying[f] \notin dropped
    /\ dropped' = dropped \cup {carrying[f]}
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![f] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, queue, fuel>>

ReturnCarry(f) ==
    /\ carrying[f] # Idle
    /\ carrying[f] \notin dropped
    /\ backlog' = backlog \cup {carrying[f]}
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![f] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, dropped, fuel>>

Refuel ==
    /\ fuel < MaxFuel
    /\ fuel' = fuel + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, queue, carrying, dropped>>

Burn ==
    /\ fuel > 0
    /\ fuel' = fuel - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, queue, carrying, dropped>>

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Targets : Enqueue(t)
    \/ \E f \in Fleets, t \in Targets : Pickup(f, t)
    \/ \E f \in Fleets : Drop(f) \/ ReturnCarry(f)
    \/ Refuel
    \/ Burn

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

DroppedFullyConsumed ==
    \A t \in dropped :
        /\ t \notin backlog
        /\ t \notin queue
        /\ \A f \in Fleets : carrying[f] # t
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Fleets = {fA, fB}
    Targets = {tg1, tg2}
    QCap = 2
    MaxFuel = 2
    Idle = Idle
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT DroppedFullyConsumed
nl:
Two independent wildfire drone fleets share one bounded dispatch queue of
targets. Releasing retardant on a target is an irreversible action that
must happen at most once per target: once a target has been hit it is
permanently consumed and leaves circulation entirely. Targets start in the
backlog. A target may be enqueued into the shared dispatch queue only while
the queue is below its capacity; when full, backpressure blocks further
enqueues. Either fleet may pick up a waiting target from the shared queue,
so the two fleets contend over the same pool. A fleet carrying a
never-hit target may drop retardant on it, which marks it dropped and
removes it from the carrying fleet without returning it anywhere, so it is
gone from the backlog, the queue, and every fleet. A fleet may instead
return an as-yet-undropped carried target to the backlog. The fleets also
manage a shared fuel level that can be topped up or burned down at any
time.

The system model has these actions: Enqueue (move a backlog target into
the shared queue while below capacity), Pickup (either fleet takes a queued
target), Drop (a fleet irreversibly hits a never-hit carried target,
consuming it out of circulation), ReturnCarry (a fleet returns an undropped
carried target to the backlog), Refuel (raise the shared fuel level), and
Burn (lower the shared fuel level).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every target that has been hit with retardant is fully
consumed -- absent from the backlog, the queue, and every fleet's grasp --
so the irreversible drop can never be applied to the same target twice.

---- MODULE W4Od6m3p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxTerm, MaxCmd, NoLeader

VARIABLES term, leader, cachedTerm, slow, cmds

vars == <<term, leader, cachedTerm, slow, cmds>>

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ cachedTerm = [n \in Nodes |-> -1]
    /\ slow = {}
    /\ cmds = 0

Elect(c) ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ c \notin slow
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ cachedTerm' = [cachedTerm EXCEPT ![c] = term + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<slow, cmds>>

StepDown ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = NoLeader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cachedTerm, slow, cmds>>

Command(c) ==
    /\ leader = c
    /\ c \notin slow
    /\ cachedTerm[c] = term
    /\ cmds < MaxCmd
    /\ cmds' = cmds + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, cachedTerm, slow>>

BecomeSlow(n) ==
    /\ n \notin slow
    /\ slow' = slow \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, cachedTerm, cmds>>

SpeedUp(n) ==
    /\ n \in slow
    /\ slow' = slow \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, cachedTerm, cmds>>

Next ==
    \/ StepDown
    \/ \E c \in Nodes : Elect(c) \/ Command(c) \/ BecomeSlow(c) \/ SpeedUp(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OnlyCurrentLeaderIsCurrent ==
    \A n \in Nodes : (cachedTerm[n] = term /\ term > 0) => (leader = n)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {e1, e2}
    MaxTerm = 3
    MaxCmd = 2
    NoLeader = NoLeader
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyCurrentLeaderIsCurrent
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper is driven by a set of controller nodes
that use leader election with failover; only the controller that is the
current-term leader is authorized to issue dispatch commands. Elections
advance a term number. When a node is elected it becomes leader and caches
the new term as the term it leads for. A leader may step down, which bumps
the term and vacates leadership, immediately making the former leader's
cached term stale (older than the new current term). A node may be slow but
never fails: while slow it cannot be elected or issue commands, but it can
always speed back up. A node may issue a dispatch command only when it is
the current leader and its cached term equals the current term, so a
controller whose leadership was superseded (holding a stale, older cached
term) or that was never elected cannot command the elevators.

The system model has these actions: Elect (a non-slow node becomes leader,
bumping the term and caching it), StepDown (the leader vacates, bumping the
term and staling the old leader), Command (the current-term leader issues a
dispatch), BecomeSlow (a node becomes temporarily slow), and SpeedUp (a
slow node recovers).

SAFETY PROPERTY: A node's cached term equals the current term only when
that node is the current leader, so no stale (superseded) or never-elected
controller can pass the authorization check to command the elevators.

---- MODULE W4Od1m4p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Aircraft, QCap, MaxBeacon

VARIABLES backlog, queue, cleared, beacon

vars == <<backlog, queue, cleared, beacon>>

Init ==
    /\ backlog = Aircraft
    /\ queue = {}
    /\ cleared = {}
    /\ beacon = 0

Enqueue(a) ==
    /\ a \in backlog
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < QCap
    /\ backlog' = backlog \ {a}
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cleared, beacon>>

Withdraw(a) ==
    /\ a \in queue
    /\ queue' = queue \ {a}
    /\ backlog' = backlog \cup {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cleared, beacon>>

ClearNormal(a) ==
    /\ a \in queue
    /\ a \notin cleared
    /\ cleared' = cleared \cup {a}
    /\ queue' = queue \ {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, beacon>>

AdminClear(a) ==
    /\ a \in backlog
    /\ a \notin cleared
    /\ cleared' = cleared \cup {a}
    /\ backlog' = backlog \ {a}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, beacon>>

Pulse ==
    /\ beacon' = (beacon + 1) % (MaxBeacon + 1)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, queue, cleared>>

Next ==
    \/ \E a \in Aircraft : Enqueue(a) \/ Withdraw(a) \/ ClearNormal(a) \/ AdminClear(a)
    \/ Pulse

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ClearedNeverPending ==
    \A a \in cleared : (a \notin backlog) /\ (a \notin queue)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Aircraft = {ac1, ac2, ac3}
    QCap = 2
    MaxBeacon = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ClearedNeverPending
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator issues takeoff clearances through a
bounded work queue with backpressure. Clearing an aircraft for takeoff is
an irreversible action that must happen at most once per aircraft; once
cleared, the aircraft is consumed out of the pending pools entirely.
Aircraft start in the backlog. An aircraft may be enqueued into the bounded
departure queue only while the queue is below its capacity; when full,
backpressure blocks further enqueues. A queued aircraft may be withdrawn
back to the backlog. The normal path clears a queued aircraft, removing it
from the queue. In addition a privileged tower-supervisor admin override
may clear an aircraft directly from the backlog, bypassing the queue
entirely. A rotating beacon pulses continuously in the background.

The system model has these actions: Enqueue (move a backlog aircraft into
the departure queue while below capacity), Withdraw (return a queued
aircraft to the backlog), ClearNormal (irreversibly clear a queued
aircraft, removing it from the queue), AdminClear (the admin override
irreversibly clears a backlog aircraft directly), and Pulse (advance the
background beacon).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every aircraft that has been cleared for takeoff is no
longer in the backlog or the departure queue, so the irreversible clearance
can never be issued to the same aircraft twice.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od19m9p5t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Books, Librarians, MaxEpoch, MaxDesk

VARIABLES epoch, available, checkedOut, libEpoch, desk

vars == <<epoch, available, checkedOut, libEpoch, desk>>

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ available = Books
    /\ checkedOut = {}
    /\ libEpoch = [l \in Librarians |-> 0]
    /\ desk = 0

Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<available, checkedOut, libEpoch, desk>>

Sync(l) ==
    /\ libEpoch[l] < epoch
    /\ libEpoch' = [libEpoch EXCEPT ![l] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, available, checkedOut, desk>>

Checkout(l, b) ==
    /\ libEpoch[l] = epoch
    /\ b \in available
    /\ checkedOut' = checkedOut \cup {b}
    /\ available' = available \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, libEpoch, desk>>

AdminCheckout(b) ==
    /\ b \in available
    /\ checkedOut' = checkedOut \cup {b}
    /\ available' = available \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, libEpoch, desk>>

DeskTick ==
    /\ desk' = (desk + 1) % (MaxDesk + 1)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, available, checkedOut, libEpoch>>

Next ==
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ DeskTick
    \/ \E l \in Librarians : Sync(l)
    \/ \E l \in Librarians, b \in Books : Checkout(l, b)
    \/ \E b \in Books : AdminCheckout(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CheckedOutNotAvailable ==
    checkedOut \cap available = {}
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Books = {bk1, bk2}
    Librarians = {lb1, lb2}
    MaxEpoch = 3
    MaxDesk = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT CheckedOutNotAvailable
nl:
A library book reservation system checks out rare books, an irreversible
action that must happen at most once per book: once a book is checked out
it leaves the available pool for good. The catalog uses epoch-numbered
reconfiguration: reconfiguring bumps the global epoch, and each librarian
must re-sync to the current epoch before processing checkouts. A librarian
synced to the current epoch may check out an available book, which moves it
from the available pool to the checked-out set. A privileged admin override
may check out an available book directly, without regard to the epoch. A
background reference desk counter ticks continuously.

The system model has these actions: Reconfigure (bump the global epoch,
staling all librarians), Sync (a stale librarian catches up to the current
epoch), Checkout (a current-epoch librarian irreversibly checks out an
available book), AdminCheckout (the admin override checks out an available
book directly), and DeskTick (advance the background reference-desk
counter).

SAFETY PROPERTY: No book is ever both checked out and still in the
available pool, so the irreversible checkout can never be applied to the
same book twice.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m3p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, Admins, MaxTerm, NoLeader

VARIABLES term, leader, acting, down

vars == <<term, leader, acting, down>>

Authorized == IF leader = NoLeader THEN Admins ELSE Admins \cup {leader}

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ acting = {}
    /\ down = {}

Elect(c) ==
    /\ leader = NoLeader
    /\ c \notin down
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = c
    /\ acting' = acting \cap Admins
    /\ UNCHANGED down

StepDown ==
    /\ leader # NoLeader
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ leader' = NoLeader
    /\ acting' = acting \cap Admins
    /\ UNCHANGED down

StartAct(c) ==
    /\ c \notin down
    /\ c \notin acting
    /\ (c = leader \/ c \in Admins)
    /\ acting' = acting \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, down>>

StopAct(c) ==
    /\ c \in acting
    /\ acting' = acting \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, down>>

Crash(c) ==
    /\ c \notin down
    /\ down' = down \cup {c}
    /\ leader' = IF leader = c THEN NoLeader ELSE leader
    /\ acting' = acting \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED term

Recover(c) ==
    /\ c \in down
    /\ down' = down \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, acting>>

Next ==
    \/ StepDown
    \/ \E c \in Nodes : Elect(c) \/ StartAct(c) \/ StopAct(c) \/ Crash(c) \/ Recover(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ActingIsAuthorized ==
    acting \subseteq Authorized
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
    Admins = {n3}
    MaxTerm = 3
    NoLeader = NoLeader
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ActingIsAuthorized
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker uses leader election with failover to
choose which node may drive matchmaking, and additionally recognizes a
fixed set of privileged admin nodes as a standing override. Only the
current-term leader or a privileged admin is authorized to be actively
matchmaking at any moment; a node that was leader in a past term but is no
longer leader is stale and must stop. Elections advance a term. When a new
leader is elected, or when the leader steps down, the term is bumped and
any actively-matchmaking node that is neither the (new) leader nor an admin
is dropped from the acting set, so a superseded leader cannot keep acting.
An authorized node -- the current leader or any admin -- may start acting,
and an acting node may stop. Any node may crash, vacating leadership if it
held it and removing it from the acting set.

bumping the term and pruning the acting set to admins), StepDown (the
leader vacates, bumping the term and pruning the acting set), StartAct (the
current leader or an admin begins matchmaking), StopAct (an acting node
stops), Crash (a node fails, vacating leadership and leaving the acting
set), and Recover (a failed node returns).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every node in the acting set is either the current leader
or a privileged admin, so no stale (superseded) or otherwise unauthorized
node is ever actively matchmaking.

whichever region it led and dropping out of the commanding set; a crashed

    /\ ch \in inService
    /\ ch \in freeChutes

    /\ queue' = queue \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<backlog, inService>>

CONSTANTS
    Bags = {b1, b2}
    Chutes = {c1, c2}
    QCap = 2
    Empty = Empty
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OccupiedChuteNotFree
nl:
An airport baggage router assigns bags to delivery chutes through a
bounded work queue with backpressure. Each chute records the bag assigned
to it or an Empty marker; a free-chute set tracks which chutes are open,
and an independent in-service set tracks which chutes are operational (not
out for maintenance). Assigning a queued bag to a free, in-service chute
stamps the chute and removes it from the free set in the same step, so a
chute that already holds a bag is never still marked free, which prevents
the same chute from being allocated to two bags. Bags start in the backlog.
A bag may be enqueued into the bounded assignment queue only while the queue
is below its capacity; a queued bag may be withdrawn back to the backlog.
Because assignment requests arrive over a reordering conveyor network,
queued bags may be assigned in any order. Releasing a chute clears its bag
back to the backlog and, if the chute is in service, returns it to the free
set. Chutes may independently be opened into service (becoming free when
empty) or, while empty, closed for maintenance.

The system model has these actions: Enqueue (queue a backlog bag while below
capacity), Withdraw (return a queued bag to the backlog), Assign (allocate a
free, in-service chute to a queued bag in any order, clearing its free bit),
Release (free a chute and return its bag to the backlog), OpenChute (bring a
chute into service, freeing it when empty), and CloseChute (take an empty
chute out of service).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any chute that currently holds a bag is not in the
free-chute set, so an occupied chute is never handed out again and no chute
is ever double allocated to two bags.

---- MODULE W4Od10m8p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Blocks, Owners, TotalTrains, Free

VARIABLES occupancy, inTransit, coarse, fine

vars == <<occupancy, inTransit, coarse, fine>>

RECURSIVE OnBlocks(_)
OnBlocks(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET b == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE IN occupancy[b] + OnBlocks(S \ {b})

Init ==
    /\ \E b \in Blocks : occupancy = [x \in Blocks |-> IF x = b THEN TotalTrains ELSE 0]
    /\ inTransit = 0
    /\ coarse = Free
    /\ fine = [b \in Blocks |-> Free]

AcquireCoarse(o) ==
    /\ coarse = Free
    /\ coarse' = o
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, inTransit, fine>>

AcquireFine(o, b) ==
    /\ coarse = o
    /\ fine[b] = Free
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = o]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, inTransit, coarse>>

Lift(o, b) ==
    /\ fine[b] = o
    /\ occupancy[b] > 0
    /\ occupancy' = [occupancy EXCEPT ![b] = @ - 1]
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>

Place(o, b) ==
    /\ fine[b] = o
    /\ inTransit > 0
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit - 1
    /\ occupancy' = [occupancy EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>

ReleaseFine(o, b) ==
    /\ fine[b] = o
    /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![b] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, inTransit, coarse>>

ReleaseCoarse(o) ==
    /\ coarse = o
    /\ \A b \in Blocks : fine[b] # o
    /\ coarse' = Free
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, inTransit, fine>>

AdminMove(f, t) ==
    /\ f # t
    /\ occupancy[f] > 0
    /\ occupancy' = [occupancy EXCEPT ![f] = @ - 1, ![t] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inTransit, coarse, fine>>

Next ==
    \/ \E o \in Owners : AcquireCoarse(o) \/ ReleaseCoarse(o)
    \/ \E o \in Owners, b \in Blocks : AcquireFine(o, b) \/ Lift(o, b) \/ Place(o, b) \/ ReleaseFine(o, b)
    \/ \E f, t \in Blocks : AdminMove(f, t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

    OnBlocks(Blocks) + inTransit = TotalTrains
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Blocks = {B1, B2}
    Owners = {o1, o2}
    TotalTrains = 2
    Free = Free
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT TrainsConserved
nl:
A subway signalling block system moves a fixed number of trains between
track blocks under hierarchical locks: an owner must first acquire the
coarse interlocking lock, then acquire a fine per-block lock, before it may
disturb a block. Trains are never created or lost; a move only lifts a
train off one block into a transit buffer and later places it back onto a
block, so the total across all blocks plus the transit buffer is constant.
Holding a block's fine lock, an owner may lift a train off that block into
transit, or place a transit train onto that block. Fine locks are released
before the coarse lock; the coarse lock may be released only once the owner
holds no fine locks. In addition a privileged admin override may move a
train directly from one block to another, bypassing the lock hierarchy
entirely, and it too conserves trains.

The system model has these actions: AcquireCoarse (take the coarse lock
when free), AcquireFine (take a block's fine lock while holding the coarse
lock), Lift (move a train from a fine-locked block into the transit
buffer), Place (move a transit train onto a fine-locked block), ReleaseFine
(release a block's fine lock), ReleaseCoarse (release the coarse lock once
no fine locks are held), and AdminMove (the override moves a train directly
between two blocks).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total number of trains on all blocks plus the number
in the transit buffer always equals the fixed fleet size, so no train is
ever created or destroyed.

CONSTANTS Nodes, Voters, Quorum, MaxMatched, NoNode

VARIABLES voteFor, inCS, requesting, matched

vars == <<voteFor, inCS, requesting, matched>>

Support(n) == Cardinality({v \in Voters : voteFor[v] = n})

Init ==
    /\ voteFor = [v \in Voters |-> NoNode]
    /\ inCS = {}
    /\ requesting = {}
    /\ matched = 0

Request(n) ==
    /\ n \notin requesting
    /\ requesting' = requesting \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<voteFor, inCS, matched>>

Grant(v, n) ==
    /\ n \in requesting
    /\ voteFor[v] = NoNode
    /\ voteFor' = [voteFor EXCEPT ![v] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, requesting, matched>>

Revoke(v) ==
    /\ voteFor[v] # NoNode
    /\ voteFor[v] \notin inCS
    /\ voteFor' = [voteFor EXCEPT ![v] = NoNode]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inCS, requesting, matched>>

Enter(n) ==
    /\ n \in requesting
    /\ n \notin inCS
    /\ Support(n) >= Quorum
    /\ inCS' = inCS \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<voteFor, requesting, matched>>

Match(n) ==
    /\ n \in inCS
    /\ matched < MaxMatched
    /\ matched' = matched + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<voteFor, inCS, requesting>>

Leave(n) ==
    /\ n \in inCS
    /\ inCS' = inCS \ {n}
    /\ requesting' = requesting \ {n}
    /\ voteFor' = [v \in Voters |-> IF voteFor[v] = n THEN NoNode ELSE voteFor[v]]
    /\ UNCHANGED matched

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Request(n) \/ Enter(n) \/ Match(n) \/ Leave(n)
    \/ \E v \in Voters, n \in Nodes : Grant(v, n)
    \/ \E v \in Voters : Revoke(v)

AuctionMutex ==
    \A a, b \in Nodes : (a \in inCS /\ b \in inCS) => (a = b)
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {x, y}
    Voters = {v1, v2, v3}
    Quorum = 2
    MaxMatched = 2
    NoNode = NoNode
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT AuctionMutex
nl:
A stock-exchange opening auction lets contending matching engines compete
for exclusive control of the single order book, arbitrated by quorum
voting. A contender first requests control; voters then grant their support
to a requesting contender. Each voter may support at most one contender at
a time, and because entry to the critical matching section requires a
quorum that exceeds half the voters, at most one contender can ever gather
enough support to enter -- this is what guarantees exclusive control. Vote
messages travel over a reordering network, so voters may grant and revoke
support in any order -- except that a voter cannot withdraw support from a
contender that is currently inside the critical section, so the winner's
mandate is locked while it controls the book. A contender with a quorum of
support enters the critical section; while inside it may match orders. On
leaving, the
contender drops its request and all of its voters' support is released.

The system model has these actions: Request (a contender starts
campaigning), Grant (a free voter supports a requesting contender, in any
order), Revoke (a voter withdraws its support), Enter (a contender holding
a quorum enters the critical matching section), Match (a contender inside
matches orders), and Leave (a contender exits, dropping its request and
releasing its voters).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one matching engine is ever inside the critical
matching section at a time, so two distinct engines never control the order
book simultaneously.

    MaxSched = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyHolderAuthorized
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler grants the exclusive right to schedule
the shared operating room by passing a single token around a ring of
surgeons. Only the current token holder, after clearing itself, is
authorized to schedule; a surgeon who passed the token on is stale and must
not schedule. Because token-pass messages travel over a hospital paging
network, they can be reordered: the holder sends the token toward another
surgeon, the message goes in flight, and in-flight pass messages may be
delivered in any order. Delivering a token makes its target the new holder
and immediately clears every authorization, so whoever was cleared before
is no longer allowed. The current holder may authorize itself, an
authorized surgeon may deauthorize, and only an authorized surgeon may
schedule an operation.

The system model has these actions: SendToken (the holder puts a token-pass
to another surgeon in flight), DeliverToken (an in-flight pass, possibly
reordered, installs a new holder and clears all authorizations), Authorize
(the current holder clears itself to schedule), Deauthorize (an authorized
surgeon steps down), and Schedule (an authorized surgeon schedules an
operation).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Only the current token holder is ever authorized to
schedule, so no stale surgeon who has passed the token on and no
unauthorized surgeon can ever schedule the operating room.

    /\ pending = Bags
    /\ routed = {}
    /\ held = {}
    /\ approvals = [b \in Bags |-> {}]
    /\ crashed = {}

    /\ se \notin crashed
    /\ b \in pending

    /\ UNCHANGED <<routed, approvals, crashed>>

    /\ b \in pending
    /\ Cardinality(approvals[b]) >= Quorum
    /\ routed' = routed \cup {b}
    /\ pending' = pending \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, approvals, crashed>>

    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {se}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, routed, held, approvals>>

nl:
An airport baggage router commits each bag to its final destination
through quorum voting -- an irreversible routing action that must happen at
most once per bag. Once a bag is routed it is consumed out of the pending
and held pools for good. Bags start pending. Each live sensor may vote to
approve a pending bag's routing; a bag is routed only once a quorum of
sensors has approved it, at which point it moves from pending into the
routed set. Independently of routing, a pending bag may be held aside for
inspection and later released back to pending, which shuffles bags between
the pending and held pools without routing them. Any sensor may crash
silently and stop voting, which only makes quorums harder to reach; a
crashed sensor may recover.

The system model has these actions: Vote (a live sensor approves a pending
bag's routing), Hold (take a pending bag aside for inspection), Release
(return a held bag to pending), Route (irreversibly route a pending bag
once a quorum approves, consuming it), Crash (a sensor fails silently), and
Recover (a crashed sensor returns).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every bag that has been routed is absent from both the
pending pool and the held pool, so the irreversible routing can never be
applied to the same bag twice.

VARIABLES balances, inTransit, stage, approvals, slow

RECURSIVE Held(_)

    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET a == CHOOSE e \in S : TRUE IN balances[a] + Held(S \ {a})

    /\ \E a \in Accounts : balances = [x \in Accounts |-> IF x = a THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ inTransit = 0
    /\ stage = "idle"
    /\ approvals = {}
    /\ slow = {}

CollectVote(v) ==
    /\ v \notin slow
    /\ v \notin approvals
    /\ approvals' = approvals \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balances, inTransit, stage, slow>>

Debit(a) ==
    /\ stage = "idle"
    /\ Cardinality(approvals) >= Quorum
    /\ balances[a] > 0
    /\ balances' = [balances EXCEPT ![a] = @ - 1]
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit + 1
    /\ stage' = "debited"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<approvals, slow>>

    /\ inTransit > 0
    /\ inTransit' = inTransit - 1
    /\ balances' = [balances EXCEPT ![a] = @ + 1]
    /\ stage' = "idle"
    /\ approvals' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED slow

BecomeSlow(v) ==
    /\ v \notin slow
    /\ slow' = slow \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balances, inTransit, stage, approvals>>

SpeedUp(v) ==
    /\ v \in slow
    /\ slow' = slow \ {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<balances, inTransit, stage, approvals>>

    \/ \E v \in Validators : CollectVote(v) \/ BecomeSlow(v) \/ SpeedUp(v)
    \/ \E a \in Accounts : Debit(a) \/ Credit(a)

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Accounts = {ac1, ac2}
    Validators = {v1, v2, v3}
    Quorum = 2
    Total = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT MoneyConserved
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement batch moves money between accounts, with
each settlement ratified by quorum voting. Money is never created or lost:
a settlement debits one unit from a source account into an in-transit
reserve and later credits it into a destination account, so the total held
across all accounts plus the in-transit reserve is always constant.
Validators vote to approve the current settlement; once a quorum has
approved, the debit step removes a unit from a source account into the
in-transit reserve, and the credit step deposits the in-transit unit into a
destination account and resets the approvals for the next settlement. A
validator may be slow but never fails: while slow it cannot vote, but it
can always speed back up, so a quorum is only delayed, never permanently
lost.

The system model has these actions: CollectVote (a non-slow validator
approves the current settlement), Debit (once a quorum approves, remove a
unit from a source account into the in-transit reserve), Credit (deposit
the in-transit unit into a destination account and reset approvals),
BecomeSlow (a validator becomes temporarily slow), and SpeedUp (a slow
validator recovers).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The total money held across all accounts plus the money in
the in-transit reserve always equals the fixed system total, so no money is
ever created or destroyed.

    /\ gen = 0

    /\ processing = {}
    /\ queueLen = 0
    /\ slow = {}

    /\ gen < MaxGen
    /\ gen' = gen + 1
    /\ processing' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<workerGen, queueLen, slow>>

    /\ w \notin slow
    /\ workerGen[w] < gen
    /\ workerGen' = [workerGen EXCEPT ![w] = gen]

    /\ w \notin processing
    /\ queueLen > 0

A subway signalling block system dispatches interlocking work to a set of
worker controllers through a bounded work queue with backpressure, and only
a worker whose authorization credential matches the current configuration
generation may process work. A worker whose credential lags the current
generation is stale and unauthorized. Reconfiguring the system bumps the
global generation and immediately halts all in-progress processing, staling

credential up to the current generation. Work arrives into the bounded

further arrivals. A worker may start processing a queued item only when it
is non-slow and its credential matches the current generation, and it later

ever processes interlocking work.

A pharmacy prescription dispenser controls exclusive access to the
controlled-substance vault through quorum voting among on-duty pharmacists.
Dispensing agents must first be registered to contend; the set of
registered agents is the system's capacity and changes at runtime as agents
are registered and deregistered. Each pharmacist may back at most one
registered agent, and entry into the vault requires a quorum of pharmacists
that exceeds half their number, so at most one agent can ever gather enough
backing to enter -- this guarantees exclusive access. A pharmacist may not
withdraw backing from an agent that is currently inside the vault, so the
winner's mandate is locked while it holds the vault. An agent with a quorum
of backing enters the vault; inside it may dispense, and on exiting it
releases all of its backing. Deregistering an agent (only while it is not in
the vault) also releases its backing.

capacity), Deregister (remove a non-vault agent, releasing its backing),

drops backing from an agent not in the vault), Enter (an agent with a quorum
enters the vault), Dispense (an agent inside the vault dispenses), and Exit
(an agent leaves the vault, releasing its backing).

SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one dispensing agent is ever inside the controlled-
substance vault at a time, so two distinct agents never access the vault
simultaneously.

CONSTANTS
    Units = {u1, u2}
    Bins = {bn1, bn2}

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker allocates blood units to storage bins
through a bounded work queue with backpressure. Each bin records the unit
stored in it or an Empty marker; an open-bin set tracks which bins are free
to receive a unit, and a separate live-bin set is the runtime capacity --
which bins are physically installed. Allocating a queued unit to a bin
stamps the bin and removes it from the open set in the same step, so a bin
that already holds a unit is never still marked open, which prevents the
same bin from being allocated to two units. Units start waiting. A unit may
be submitted into the bounded queue only while it is below capacity, and a
queued unit may be cancelled back to waiting. Freeing a bin clears its unit
back to waiting and, if the bin is live, returns it to the open set. Bins
may be added to the live capacity (becoming open when empty) or, while
empty, removed from the capacity.

capacity), Cancel (return a queued unit to waiting), Allocate (store a
queued unit into a free, live bin, clearing the bin's open bit), Free (empty
a bin and return its unit to waiting), AddBin (install a bin into the live
capacity, opening it when empty), and RemoveBin (uninstall an empty bin).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any bin that currently holds a blood unit is not in the
open-bin set, so an occupied bin is never handed out again and no bin is
ever double allocated to two units.

nl:
A print-shop job spooler commits print jobs under hierarchical locks: an
owner must first take the coarse printer lock, then take a fine per-tray
lock, before it can print. Printing a job is an irreversible action that
must happen at most once per job: once printed, a job is consumed out of

be held aside for proofing and later released back to pending, independent
of printing. Holding a tray's fine lock (which requires already holding the
coarse lock), an owner prints a pending job, moving it into the printed set.
Fine locks are released before the coarse lock. The set of online trays is
the runtime capacity and changes: a tray may be added online, or, while its
fine lock is free, removed.

The system model has these actions: Hold (take a pending job aside for
proofing), Release (return a held job to pending), AcquireCoarse (take the
coarse lock when free), AcquireFine (take an online tray's fine lock while
holding the coarse lock), Print (irreversibly print a pending job using a
fine-locked tray, consuming it), ReleaseFine (release a tray's fine lock),
ReleaseCoarse (release the coarse lock once no fine locks are held), AddTray
(bring a tray online, growing capacity), and RemoveTray (take an
unlocked tray offline, shrinking capacity).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every job that has been printed is absent from both the
pending pool and the held pool, so the irreversible print can never be
applied to the same job twice.

actually been applied to the shared wash program, so no acknowledged update
is ever lost.

A stock-exchange opening auction allocates trading seats to traders using
lease-based ownership with expiry. Each seat's holder field records the
trader that holds it or a Free marker; a free-seat set tracks which seats

currently in service. A global clock ticks forward. Allocating a free,
online seat to a trader stamps the seat with the trader and a lease
deadline, and removes it from the free set in the same step, so a seat that

from being allocated to two traders. A holder may renew its lease deadline.

brought online (becoming free when unheld) or, while unheld, taken offline,
changing the capacity at runtime.

double allocated to two traders.

CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2}
    MaxTerm = 2
    MaxServe = 2
    NoLeader = NoLeader
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT OnlyCurrentLeaderCached
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser cluster uses leader election with
failover; only the current-term leader is authorized to dispense. Elections
advance a term. When a node is elected it becomes leader and a leadership
announcement tagged with the new term is queued for delivery. Because
announcements travel over a reordering network, they may be delivered in
any order, and stale announcements from earlier terms may surface late. A
node caches the term from whatever announcement it receives. A node may
dispense only when it is the current leader and its cached term equals the
current term, so a node holding a stale cached term (from a reordered old
announcement) or that was never elected cannot dispense. A leader may step
down, bumping the term and vacating leadership.

The system model has these actions: Elect (a node becomes leader, bumping
the term and queuing a leadership announcement), StepDown (the leader
vacates, bumping the term), DeliverAnnounce (an announcement, possibly
reordered, sets a node's cached term), StaleAnnounce (a delayed
earlier-term announcement resurfaces on the network), and Dispense (the
current-term leader dispenses).

SAFETY PROPERTY: A node's cached term equals the current term only when
that node is the current leader, so no stale or never-elected node can ever
pass the authorization check to dispense.

    /\ queue = {}
    /\ handledBy = [r \in Requests |-> NoLib]
    /\ slow = {}

    /\ shift < MaxShift
    /\ shift' = shift + 1
    /\ handledBy' = [r \in Requests |-> NoLib]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<credEpoch, queue, slow>>

Renew(l) ==
    /\ l \notin slow
    /\ credEpoch[l] < shift
    /\ credEpoch' = [credEpoch EXCEPT ![l] = shift]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shift, queue, handledBy, slow>>

Enqueue(r) ==
    /\ r \notin queue
    /\ handledBy[r] = NoLib
    /\ Cardinality(queue) < QCap
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shift, credEpoch, handledBy, slow>>

StartHandle(l, r) ==
    /\ l \notin slow
    /\ credEpoch[l] = shift
    /\ r \in queue
    /\ handledBy[r] = NoLib
    /\ handledBy' = [handledBy EXCEPT ![r] = l]
    /\ queue' = queue \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shift, credEpoch, slow>>

Finish(r) ==
    /\ handledBy[r] # NoLib
    /\ handledBy' = [handledBy EXCEPT ![r] = NoLib]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shift, credEpoch, queue, slow>>

BecomeSlow(l) ==
    /\ l \notin slow
    /\ slow' = slow \cup {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shift, credEpoch, queue, handledBy>>

SpeedUp(l) ==
    /\ l \in slow
    /\ slow' = slow \ {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<shift, credEpoch, queue, handledBy>>

    \/ \E r \in Requests : Enqueue(r) \/ Finish(r)

nl:
A library book reservation system dispatches reservation requests to
librarians through a bounded work queue with backpressure, and only a
librarian holding a credential for the current shift may handle a request.
A librarian whose credential is from an earlier shift is stale and
unauthorized. A shift change bumps the shift number and clears every
in-progress handling, so a librarian credentialed for an old shift can no
longer be handling anything until it renews. A librarian may renew its
credential up to the current shift. A request may be enqueued into the
bounded queue only while it is below capacity and not already being handled.
A librarian may start handling a queued request only when it is non-slow and
its credential matches the current shift; a handled request is later
finished. A librarian may be slow but never fails: while slow it cannot
renew or handle, but it can always speed back up.

The system model has these actions: ShiftChange (bump the shift, clearing
all in-progress handling and staling every credential), Renew (a non-slow
librarian refreshes its credential to the current shift), Enqueue (queue a
request while below capacity), StartHandle (a non-slow, current-shift
librarian takes a queued request), Finish (a librarian finishes a handled
request), BecomeSlow (a librarian becomes temporarily slow), and SpeedUp (a
slow librarian recovers).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every request currently being handled is handled by a
librarian whose credential equals the current shift, so no stale or
unauthorized librarian ever handles a reservation request.
